method: method of analogues in delay-embedded solar coordinates, calibrated by local divergence tercile
price_models: gravity + tidal (short pendulum restoring, long pendulum momentum, sector carried to its companies)
caveats: Origins before CY2015Q1 are an in-sample warm-up: the coordinates' typical spreads (the analogue metric) were measured on data through that period. Scorecards start there.

Sector suns and the market centre are rebuilt as of each period (clip bounds over the periods up to then, weights = revenue reported by then), but the companies are today's: firms that left the market are missing from the early years (survivorship), which flatters every model.
note: Each arrow: where the dot's next period lands on average among the most similar past states (any company, position and velocity), shrunk toward no move by how well such arrows did before. lam: local divergence of those analogues (log ratio per step; higher = they fan out = less predictable). Not a Lyapunov exponent and not proof of chaos. The price coordinate (stock vs the S&P) and the price come from the gravity + tidal model where it covers the company (price_model 1), otherwise from the analogues: close x exp(forecast vs the S&P + the S&P's past average). Origins before the last are walk-forward backtest forecasts whose analogue library held only steps public at the time; see caveats for what is still retrospective.
